conviction_note: Small positive lean: the H1 plan (OP 6.0bn yen, NP 4.0bn) was already 73%/79% covered after Q1 and the company has revised its full-year forecast at every Q2 print since 2022, upward in both 2024 and 2025, against an IFIS consensus that is simply the company plan; partly offset by weak Toyota-group read-through from 10/28 and the company's own Q1 warning of a 'tens of billions of yen' purchased-goods headwind, so p_up 57 on a 4.0% scale gives +0.56, while the findings sum to +1.2 because each is sized alone and the revision finding carries its own size.
bar: H1 company plan published 2026-04-28 and held at Q1: H1 revenue 151.9bn, OP 6.0bn, pretax 7.0bn, NP 4.0bn; FY revenue 310bn, OP 17.5bn, pretax 18.5bn, NP 11.3bn, dividend 150 yen (https://kabutan.jp/stock/news?code=5482&b=k202607310112). IFIS consensus (https://kabuyoho.jp/sp/reportAnalyst?bcode=5482, 2026-10-28) carries FY pretax 18.5bn, OP 17.5bn, NP 11.3bn, identical to the company plan, with revenue at 323bn, so there is no separate street number. print_vs_bar_pct is H1 OP vs the 6.0bn H1 plan, assuming Q2 OP of about 3.5-4.5bn (Q1 was 4.36bn). That beat is visible to anyone from the Q1 progress rate.
positioning_check: JPX disclosed short register: 0.0% (no position at or above 0.5%), unchanged, as of 2026-10-28 (https://www.jpx.co.jp/markets/public/short-selling/index.html via the baseline). Margin (kabutan, https://kabutan.jp/stock/?code=5482, week of 10/23): margin short 35.8k shares against margin long 155.4k, ratio 4.34, down from 8.75 on 10/09 because the margin short balance doubled from 17.6k to 35.8k in two weeks. In absolute terms that is small, about 0.2 days of the roughly 180k shares/day the 20-day median turnover implies. No options or skew exist. The 20-day run-up is -7.43% and the 5-day run-up -1.51%, and priced_lean_pct is +0.05, so the lean is close to neutral.

findings.finding: The company has revised its full-year forecast at every Q2 print (2022-10-28, 2023-10-31, 2024-10-31, 2025-10-31), upward in 2024 (NP +73%, dividend +70 yen pre-split) and 2025 (NP 9.5bn to 10.0bn, dividend 134 to 138 yen). This year's H1 plan (OP 6.0bn, NP 4.0bn) was already 73%/79% achieved by Q1 (OP 4.36bn, NP 3.17bn) and is the same 6.0bn H1 OP plan that was beaten at 8.78bn last year. A full-year revision is likely at this release and leans upward. Under the dividend policy (a regular dividend at 40% of NP plus a fixed 5.0bn yen special), any NP raise lifts the dividend mechanically.

FY print 2026-04-28 (dividend raise) +7.26%. Q1 2026-07-31 (FY held, raw-material warning) -3.74%. Yahoo daily bars, https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/5482.T?range=3y&interval=1d

findings.why_not_priced: IFIS consensus sits exactly on the company plan (pretax 18.5bn on 10/28, unchanged for 4 weeks), so no analyst number has priced a raise. The stock is down 7.4% over 20 sessions and 12% from its pre-Q1 close of 3,185, which is the price of a market expecting a hold or trim rather than a raise. If a raise were priced, the consensus would sit above plan and the stock would not have bled into the print. The progress rate itself is public, so only the revision decision is new.
findings.independence: Partly shares a document with finding 2 (the Q1 supplementary deck sets both the H1 base and the raw-material caveat). Dividend formula from the 2026-04-28 dividend notice https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260428/140120260424510140.pdf (regular dividend at 40% payout plus a 5.0bn special).

findings.finding: Q1 operating profit carried a slide-gap headwind of -2.7bn yen (from +0.3bn a year earlier): surcharges pass purchased-goods prices through with a one-half or one-quarter lag. Tokyo Steel's H2 scrap purchase price then fell from 50,500-53,000 yen/t (Jul 29) to 47,000-50,000 (Aug 21), so Q2/H2 margins should get some of that gap back. Partly offset by the Q1 +1.2bn inventory gain, which reverses as scrap falls.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026-07-31: the deck flagged a purchased-goods headwind of 'tens of billions of yen' against plan with the FY held; the stock fell 7.2% on the day after the 14:40 release and rebounded 4.4% the next day (Yahoo bars).
findings.why_not_priced: The scrap decline is public, but transmitting it into Aichi's Q2 slide gap means reading the surcharge-lag footnote in the deck. With the consensus sitting on the plan, nobody has published that margin recovery. If it were priced, the stock would not be trading below its Q1-reaction low area (2,956 close on 7/31) on a 5.3% yield. This is a proxy plus an inference, sized small.
findings.independence: Scrap series from a different source: SteelOrbis, https://www.steelorbis.com/steel-prices/steel-prices-market-analyses/scrap-and-raw-materials/tokyo-steel-cuts-h2-scrap-purchase-price-by-jpy-1000mt-1472247.htm (snippet_only; date from the search summary, August 2026).

Toyota's August global production was -5.9% and domestic -1.7%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean history of this name reacting to peer read-through; the 2026-10-28 session (peer day) closed 2,830, -0.8% (Yahoo bars).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: the peer releases were public from 14:20-14:40 on 10/28, and 5482 closed -0.8% that day and was -0.6% at the seal. Aichi's Q1 volume was +7% yoy and its mix is domestic Toyota steel and forgings, so the Chuo Spring causes (China, NA tariffs, company investment) transmit only partly. Kept small.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: likely (revised at every Q2 since 2022; the H1 plan is already 73% covered on OP), leaning up, with a hold possible given the Q1 raw-material warning; the street (IFIS) equals the plan. Returns: the dividend is formulaic (40% of NP regular plus a fixed 5.0bn special), so a raise adds a few yen; no buyback history at Q2. New-year guide: n/a (H1 print). Quarter vs own 進捗率: H1 OP will beat the 6.0bn plan by about 2-3bn (last year 8.78 vs 6.0); NP progress after Q1 was 79.3% against a 5-year average of 70.1%, and that is public.

baseline_tension: The lean is mildly positive while the tape is negative (-7.4% over 20 days, margin shorts building) and the baseline lean is about neutral (+0.05), so the finding cuts slightly against the run-up. The strongest negative the release could carry is a held FY that implies an H2 decline, or a trim citing the raw-material headwind flagged at Q1; peers on 10/28 show that is possible. The strongest positive, an upward revision plus a dividend raise, was searched for and is supported by four years of Q2 revisions.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on a series the market already has): the Toyota-group read-through negative was public from 14:20-14:40 on 10/28 and already traded (-0.8% that day), so it shrank from -0.6 to -0.4; p_up unchanged because the overall lean is positive, not negative.
Rule 2 (check the sign): the set leans positive; baseline_tension now records the strongest negative and the strongest positive and confirms both were searched for. Nothing else changed.
